A: Discover the distinct purposes of all supplied Git changes before assigning files. Each purpose must describe one concrete changed behavior or contract and its affected symbol or target. Combine matching implementation, tests and consumers for the same purpose. Separate independently reversible changes even in the same directory or file. Shared imports, helpers or packages alone do not prove one purpose. Describe only changes grounded in supplied evidence; do not invent author requirements or claim unseen prior behavior. Return a short English description and a unique sequential purpose ID P001, P002, etc.
B:
Identify distinct change purposes from the supplied Git changes.

Group changes that implement, test, or consume the same
behavioral change or shared contract.

Do not create separate purposes for different parts of
the same behavioral change.

Separate changes only when they represent independent
behavioral goals. Sharing a file, package, import, or helper
is not sufficient evidence of a shared purpose.

Describe each purpose using only concrete changes
supported by the input. Do not infer unseen requirements
or behavior.

Return a concise description and a unique purpose ID
for each distinct purpose.
C:
Identify distinct change purposes from the supplied Git changes.

Group changes that contribute to the same behavioral
change or contract, including related implementations,
tests, and consumers.

Separate changes with independent purposes.

Describe each purpose using only evidence from the input.

Return a concise description and a unique purpose ID
